newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST - Solid but slower H1 seen for CRH.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Solid but slower H1 seen for CRH.

text.p: Building materials group CRH Plc should post solid half-year results on Wednesday although growth will be slower than in recent years as bad weather and a weaker European market take their toll, analysts said.

Irish analysts said they expected pre-tax profits of around 62 to 66 million Irish pounds, up from 56.9 million in the first half last year. But the bulk of the year's profits will come in the second half, when growth will be stronger, they said.
"The first half will not be particularly memorable in terms of pre-tax profits," said Davy Stockbrokers analyst Joe Burnell.
"But we'd still expect CRH to show some progress," he said.
Burnell said he expected pre-tax profits of 62 million Irish pounds for the first six months of 1996. He forecast earnings per share of just over 13.5 pence versus 12.8 pence a year ago.

"A lot of CRH's counterparts have been signalling a fairly weak first half," Burnell said. "Certainly it would have started off weather-affected and there has been a slowdown in capital investment, in mainland Europe particularly. The UK has been weak as well."
Goodbody Stockbrokers analyst David Lowe forecast pre-tax profits of 65.2 million and earnings per share of 14.2 pence.

"The German market has clearly been slowing and that will affect other European markets also," he said. "CRH have been cautious on Europe and it will be interesting to see what they have to say about the second half."
Lowe said acquisitions would have little effect on first-half profits. "Most of the acquisitions won't be kicking-in much in the first half," he said.

Analysts said the second half would be considerably stronger. "CRH is always much stronger in the second half, particularly in the U.S.," Lowe said. "The contribution from acquisitions will be feeding through then too."
Burnell also said the second half would see stronger growth. "Obviously there will be some pick-up weatherwise, and the U.S. has done pretty well in recent months," he said.

"Ireland will be good and the UK should be a little bit better in the second half as well, and you've got the acquisitions coming through," Burnell said. "So the second half should be a fair bit better."

Analysts said the results statement would also be closely scrutinised for any hints regarding the possible acquisition of BTR's U.S. unit Tilcon. The Financial Times said last week that CRH was discussing the purchase of Tilcon for about 180 million stg.
